bindings.previous_target: 如果你曾真心在乎我，如果你曾觉得我值得你花时间……那就与我一同留在这里，在虚无的寂静中永远安息吧。

bindings.source: If it would purchase her one single shred of happiness, I would overlook nearly anything in the world for Gerta.
bindings.previous_target: 但只要能为她换来哪怕一丝幸福，为了格尔塔，这世上几乎任何事我都可以不计较。

bindings.source: If only Astrid was still alive, or haunted these walls as I, we could ask her.
bindings.previous_target: 要是阿斯特丽德还活着，或者像我一样以幽灵之身徘徊在这城堡里，我们就能问问她了。

bindings.source: If only Astrid was still alive, or haunted these walls as I, we could ask her.
bindings.previous_target: 要是阿斯特丽德还活着，或是像我一样在这座城堡里游荡，我们就能问问她了。

bindings.source: If only I had known the kind of strength you possess when I was alive, child.
bindings.previous_target: 孩子，要是我活着的时候就知道你拥有这样的力量，该多好。

bindings.source: If only I had known the kind of strength you possess when I was alive, child.
bindings.previous_target: 孩子，要是我生前就知道你有这样的力量，该多好。

bindings.source: If she could not give me an heir, she could not fulfill her duties as Queen, as she saw them. And to her, that was the gravest failing of all.
bindings.previous_target: 在她看来，如果不能为我生下继承人，就无法履行王后的职责。而对她而言，这是最严重的失职。

bindings.source: If she could not give me an heir, she could not fulfill her duties as Queen, as she saw them. And to her, that was the gravest failing of all.
bindings.previous_target: 在她看来，如果不能为我生下继承人，她就无法尽到自己认定的王后职责。而对她来说，那是最严重的失职。

bindings.source: If this is the future you desire, choose it with intent, Ophelia.
bindings.previous_target: 如果这就是你想要的未来，奥菲莉娅，那就明确地选择它。

bindings.source: If this is the future you desire, choose it with intent, Ophelia.
bindings.previous_target: 如果这就是你想要的未来，就明确地选择它，奥菲莉娅。

bindings.source: If you choose this world, go into it gladly. Do not let the inevitable pain rob the intensity of your love.
bindings.previous_target: 如果你选择这个世界，就欣然走进去。别让不可避免的痛苦消磨你炽热的爱意。

bindings.source: If you choose this world, go into it gladly. Do not let the inevitable pain rob the intensity of your love.

bindings.previous_target: 如果你再次回到埃尔西诺，就会再次失去关于你刚刚选择的命运的一切记忆，也无法再选择它。换句话说……

bindings.source: If you return to Elsinore again, you will again lose all memory of the fate you just chose, and you will not be able to choose it again. In other words...
bindings.previous_target: 如果你再次回到埃尔西诺，你又会失去关于刚刚所选命运的一切记忆，也再不能选择它。换句话说……

bindings.source: Impossible to tell. My mother is long dead.
bindings.previous_target: 无从得知。我的母亲已经死去很久了。

bindings.source: Impossible to tell. My mother is long dead.
bindings.previous_target: 无从知晓。我的母亲早已去世。

bindings.source: In a manner of speaking. Quince is the one who kept me in that shadowy version of Elsinore. I knew Claudius was trying to murder me from the start. But...
bindings.previous_target: 可以这么说。是昆斯把我困在了那个阴暗的埃尔西诺里。我从一开始就知道克劳狄斯想谋杀我。但是……

bindings.source: In a manner of speaking. Quince is the one who kept me in that shadowy version of Elsinore. I knew Claudius was trying to murder me from the start. But...
bindings.previous_target: 从某种意义上说，是的。把我困在那个阴暗的埃尔西诺里的，就是昆斯。我从一开始就知道克劳狄斯想谋杀我。可是……

bindings.source: In another, Claudius created a conspiracy, then convinced my own men to turn against me and have me imprisoned indefinitely.
bindings.previous_target: 在另一个世界里，克劳狄斯策划了一场阴谋，又说服我的部下反叛我，把我关了起来，永不释放。

bindings.source: In another, Claudius created a conspiracy, then convinced my own men to turn against me and have me imprisoned indefinitely.
bindings.previous_target: 在另一个世界里，克劳狄斯策划了一场阴谋，随后说服我自己的部下背叛我，把我关了起来，永无出头之日。

bindings.source: In life, I did not fight Insanity. I relinquished myself to her. I was subjugated, consumed, and finally death took me.
bindings.previous_target: 生前，我没有与疯狂抗争。我把自己交给了她。我被她征服、吞噬，最终死亡带走了我。

bindings.source: In plain sight of all, and accessible to those curious enough to find it.

bindings.source: In plain sight of all, and accessible to those curious enough to find it.
bindings.previous_target: 就在所有人眼前，只要有足够的好奇心去寻找，就能找到。

bindings.source: In that case, I am at your service.

bindings.previous_target: 既然如此，我愿为你效劳。

bindings.source: Indeed. I am that body once called King Hamlet.
bindings.previous_target: 正是。我就是那个曾被称为哈姆雷特国王的人。

bindings.previous_target: 确实。我可以显形，虽然很困难。

bindings.previous_target: 从上次见到你，到现在这次醒来，我感觉只过了一瞬。那我想，我应该一直在等你吧。

bindings.previous_target: 从上次见到你，到此刻醒来，感觉只过了一瞬。那么，我想我一定是在等你。

bindings.source: It has lingered long past its due.

bindings.source: It has lingered long past its due.
bindings.previous_target: 它早就该结束了，却拖延至今。

bindings.source: It is a sleep which one has no memory of entering.

bindings.source: It is a sleep which one has no memory of entering.
bindings.previous_target: 那是一场沉睡，你不会记得自己是如何睡去的。

bindings.source: It is a trick invented by your own mind.
bindings.previous_target: 这是你自己的头脑编造出来的骗局。

bindings.previous_target: 这是你自己的头脑编造出来的骗局。

bindings.source: It is eternally more worthwhile to fight than to give up as I did, Ophelia. Never forget that. For you, hope lingers.
bindings.previous_target: 奥菲莉娅，抗争永远比像我这样放弃更有意义。永远别忘了这一点。你仍有希望。

bindings.source: It is impossible, yes. It is the rules of the larger game.

bindings.source: It is shattered. Gone. And once you set foot back in Elsinore, you will lose all memory of what you chose.
bindings.previous_target: 它已经破碎。消失了。而一旦你重新踏入埃尔西诺，就会失去关于自己所选命运的一切记忆。

bindings.source: It is strange, how these matters bear forth.
bindings.previous_target: 世事如此发展，真是奇妙。

bindings.source: It is strange, how these matters bear forth.
bindings.previous_target: 这些事竟会这样发展，真是奇怪。

bindings.source: It is tempting to flee responsibility for the lives of those you love.

bindings.previous_target: 终点到了。

bindings.source: It is the oldest, most primal power of humankind.
bindings.previous_target: 那是人类最古老、最原始的力量。

bindings.source: It is.
bindings.previous_target: 是我。

bindings.source: It shall not end until Elsinore lies silent.
bindings.previous_target: 直到埃尔西诺归于死寂，这一切才会结束。

bindings.source: It shall not end until Elsinore lies silent.
bindings.previous_target: 直到埃尔西诺归于死寂，这一切才会结束。

bindings.previous_target: 现在回头还来得及！

bindings.previous_target: 这是死者最擅长的事。

bindings.source: It's what the dead do best.

bindings.source: Leaving out the gash in your neck when they tell the tale.

bindings.source: Let me give you what you came here for. We have nothing more to say to one another, after all.

bindings.source: Let me give you what you desire, then. The chance to find something else. Something 'better.'
bindings.previous_target: 那就让我给你想要的东西吧。一个寻找别的可能的机会。寻找“更好的”可能。

bindings.source: Let me give you what you desire, then. The chance to find something else. Something 'better.'
bindings.previous_target: 那就让我给你想要的吧。一个寻找别的命运的机会。某种“更好”的命运。

bindings.source: Let us go away now, Ophelia. Forever.
bindings.previous_target: 我们走吧，奥菲莉娅。永远离开。

bindings.source: Let us go away now, Ophelia. Forever.
bindings.previous_target: 我们走吧，奥菲莉娅。永远离开。

bindings.source: Life in place of death is not always a gift. You and I know that truest of all.

bindings.source: Life in place of death is not always a gift. You and I know that truest of all.
bindings.previous_target: 以生代死，并不总是一份恩赐。你我比谁都清楚这一点。

bindings.source: Most live life without ever experiencing such a thing. I certainly did. So shall many of these good people before us.
bindings.previous_target: 大多数人终其一生都不曾体验过这样的幸福。我便是如此。我们面前的这些好人，许多也会如此。

bindings.source: Most live life without ever experiencing such a thing. I certainly did. So shall many of these good people before us.

bindings.source: Most ordinary folk choose love not knowing where the future might lead.
bindings.previous_target: 大多数普通人选择去爱时，都不知道未来会走向何方。

bindings.source: Most ordinary folk choose love not knowing where the future might lead.
bindings.previous_target: 大多数普通人选择去爱时，并不知道未来会走向何方。

bindings.source: My brother lives.
bindings.previous_target: 我的弟弟还活着。

bindings.source: My form is feeble. I feel my flesh disintegrating. I must go.
bindings.previous_target: 我的形体很虚弱。我感觉自己的血肉正在崩解。我必须走了。

bindings.source: My form is feeble. I feel my flesh disintegrating. I must go.
bindings.previous_target: 我的形体很虚弱。我感到自己的血肉正在消散。我必须走了。

bindings.previous_target: 我的记忆像雾一样飘散。去你父亲那里取回我最后写下的东西。也许到那时，我们就能弄明白这片虚无。

bindings.source: My memories drift away like fog. Retrieve my final writings from your father. Perhaps then we can make sense of this nothingness.
bindings.previous_target: 我的记忆像雾一样飘散。从你父亲那里取回我最后写下的那些文字。也许到那时，我们就能从这片空白中理出头绪。

bindings.source: My notes—my notes, taken by him, out of love, out of protection—

bindings.source: My notes—my notes, taken by him, out of love, out of protection—

bindings.source: My son cannot see me any longer. He seems to have no memory of ever meeting me.
bindings.previous_target: 我儿子已经看不见我了。他似乎完全不记得自己曾见过我。

bindings.source: My son cannot see me any longer. He seems to have no memory of ever meeting me.
bindings.previous_target: 我的儿子已经看不见我了。他似乎完全不记得曾经见过我。

bindings.source: My son, listen carefully to me.
bindings.previous_target: 我的儿子，仔细听我说。

bindings.source: My son, listen carefully to me.
bindings.previous_target: 儿子，仔细听我说。

bindings.previous_target: 我的儿子。记住我生前告诉你的话：必须坚持争取胜利，直到所有可能的办法都用尽。

bindings.source: My son. Remember what I told you in life: One must prevail until no other possible method remains.
bindings.previous_target: 我的儿子。记住我生前对你说过的话：只要还有办法，就必须坚持到底。

bindings.source: My son... the darkness which unfolded within him in these past months has been buried, but not truly forgotten.
bindings.previous_target: 我的儿子……过去几个月里，他心中滋生的黑暗已被埋藏，却并未真正被遗忘。

bindings.source: My son... the darkness which unfolded within him in these past months has been buried, but not truly forgotten.
bindings.previous_target: 我的儿子……过去几个月里在他心中蔓延的黑暗，虽然被埋藏了，却并没有真正被遗忘。

bindings.source: My wife has suffered enough in this life. Improper though it may be for a man to allow his wife to be wooed by his brother...
bindings.previous_target: 我的妻子这一生已经受够了苦。纵容自己的兄弟追求自己的妻子，对一个男人来说或许有失体统……

bindings.source: My wife has suffered enough in this life. Improper though it may be for a man to allow his wife to be wooed by his brother...
bindings.previous_target: 我的妻子这一生已经受够了苦。虽说一个男人容许自己的兄弟向妻子求爱，或许有违礼法……

bindings.source: Never again will you settle down with Lady Guildenstern and Lady Rosencrantz, though you had found peace with them.

bindings.source: Never again will you settle down with Lady Guildenstern and Lady Rosencrantz, though you had found peace with them.
bindings.previous_target: 你曾与吉尔登斯吞女士和罗森克兰兹女士一起找到了安宁，却将再也无法和她们一同安定下来。

bindings.source: Nevertheless, I will show you the way back to Elsinore.
bindings.previous_target: 不过，我还是会为你指出回埃尔西诺的路。

bindings.source: Nevertheless, I will show you the way back to Elsinore.
bindings.previous_target: 尽管如此，我还是会为你指明回埃尔西诺的路。

bindings.source: Next time around, perhaps, will be different.
bindings.previous_target: 也许下一次，会有所不同。

bindings.previous_target: 无论男女，都不能因此责怪你。

bindings.source: No man or woman could lay blame with you.
bindings.previous_target: 没有人能责怪你。

bindings.previous_target: 那种永享幸福的世界并不存在。对你如此，对世上任何人都如此。

bindings.previous_target: 永远幸福的世界并不存在。对你如此，对世上任何人都如此。

bindings.source: No, Ophelia. There is no other way.
bindings.previous_target: 不，奥菲莉娅。没有别的办法。

bindings.previous_target: 没有，奥菲莉娅。没有别的办法了。

bindings.source: No, no. There is something you do not understand about the threads of fate, I think. They are woven together as one, a transcendent tapestry.
bindings.previous_target: 不，不。我想，关于命运的丝线，有些事你还不明白。它们交织为一体，成为一幅超越凡俗的织锦。

bindings.source: No. Impossible. Quince encouraged me to find the Book of Fates.
bindings.previous_target: 不。不可能。昆斯曾鼓励我去寻找《命运之书》。

bindings.previous_target: 不。不可能。昆斯曾鼓励我寻找《命运之书》。

bindings.source: No. It makes it 'nothing.' Neither right nor wrong. It is meaningless. Rid yourself of guilt. You will need all wits about you if you are to prevail.

bindings.source: No. Not the war.

No.
bindings.previous_target: 不。

bindings.previous_target: 那么，你带来了什么消息？

No--

bindings.previous_target: 我当然认识他，可我有什么好怕的？

bindings.source:
I remember Celeste rode in the front.

She was the head of the May parade, wearing a long white dress with a blue ribbon around her waist and flowers braided into her hair. No one had ever seen a May Queen half so pretty, they said. A trail of wagons tied together proceeded down the only street in town and there she sat at the very front, skirts trailing beneath her legs, which dangled off the wagon's edge. Her feet were bare and pale and clean, her eyes a blue to match her sash. And even I had to admit she was beautiful.

I watched her go by from just outside mum's cottage. She turned to smile at me and called out. 'Anna! Come dance with us!' She extended her hands towards me, the bells tied to her wrists tinkling faintly. We had been best friends once, after all.

But the boys who walked at her side jeered at me. 'Ugly little bitch!' one of them screeched. Another tossed a stone. 'Brown-toothed, slack-jawed, scruff-haired nothing!' One of them came after me with a stick, as though he meant to break it over my back.

Tears filling my eyes, I retreated into the woods. Far away from the raucous sounds of the May Day parade, everything here was dark and silent. The trees stretched like fingers overhead, and for a moment I forgot myself in that darkness. I knew not where I went, but walked with my eyes locked upon the mossy ground. There was no path. I needed none.

All humans know when they have truly become lost. And so I had. It was nearly midnight now, though it had been noon when I left my mother's threshold. A full moon lit my path, casting twining shadows on the forest floor. 

At last I came upon a still lake. And there I prayed to the spirit of spring herself, that great goddess whose image all May Queens were created in. 'Make me beautiful like Celeste,' I cried. 'Make me worthy of being the May Queen, too!'

The waters parted. A single wave lapped the surface. And then, slowly, the mare climbed out of the water's depths, one hoof at a time. It was a white mare, drenched through, and it shook its head wildly, flicking drops of water from its mane. Surely this must be the goddess herself, manifested in mortal form. Its mane was braided -- just as Celeste's had been -- but with mossweed, not flowers.

The mare stood before me, its golden eyes fixed upon me. At last it said (with no mouth that could move, but with a voice all the same) 'Child of man, have you come to seek my aid?'

'I have,' I said, quietly. 'I want to be beautiful. As beautiful as Celeste.'

It bowed its great head to me and nuzzled my hand. I touched it tenderly, its breath on my fingers. And, flooded with sudden relief that my prayer had been answered, I pressed my face into its mane and sobbed.

'Cry not, child of man,' it told me. 'Come into my dark waters and be reborn as a goddess in your own right. Merely climb on my back, and we'll descend together. You shall be a May Queen yet.'

I wrapped its mane round my fingers and pulled myself up her back with all my might, swinging one leg over her sinewy side. Together, we began to descend into the water. I felt the cold bite of it weighing down my skirts, my shoes; and before I knew it, the water was up to my chest. 

It was then I peered beneath the surface and my heart leapt into my chest. The mare was no mare, but a rotted, hulking thing, its flesh stripped in pieces from its corpse and fluttering in the water's current. The wet stink of death came upon me, and I gagged. I reached for the only thing I could grab -- a branch overhanging the pond -- and pulled with all my might. The creature ceased its descent beneath the water and turned upon me, its face little more than two shriveled eyes in a grinning skull.

A name rose to my lips, a choked scream. 'Brook horse!'

'Yesssss,' the thing in the water hissed. Its horselike lips pulled back, revealing sharpened teeth.

I turned to swim, but felt those teeth closing down upon my back. The moon grew small, high above the surface, fading from reach. The soft green of it all surrounded me. I sank down to the moss at the bottom. No. Not moss. Remains. And the last thing I saw was that sharp, grinning smile.

'You shall never be Queen,' it rasped. 'But your bones shall be beautiful indeed.'
bindings.previous_target:
我记得塞莱斯特坐在最前面。

她领着五月节的游行队伍，身穿白色长裙，腰间系着蓝丝带，头发里编着鲜花。大家说，从没见过哪位五月女王有她一半漂亮。一辆辆相连的马车沿着镇上唯一的街道前行，她就坐在最前头，裙摆垂在腿下，双腿悬在车沿外。她光着脚，双脚白净，眼睛和腰间的丝带一样蓝。就连我也不得不承认，她很美。

我站在妈妈的小屋外，看着她经过。她转过头，对我微笑着喊道：“安娜！来跟我们一起跳舞吧！”她朝我伸出双手，系在手腕上的铃铛轻轻作响。毕竟，我们曾经是最好的朋友。

可走在她身旁的男孩们却嘲笑我。“丑八怪，小贱人！”其中一个尖声叫道。另一个扔来一块石头。“黄牙、呆脸、乱毛的废物！”还有一个拿着棍子朝我追来，像是要往我背上打，直到把棍子打断。

泪水盈满了我的眼睛，我退进树林。这里远离五月节游行的喧闹，一切都幽暗而寂静。树木像手指一样伸展在头顶，一时间，我在黑暗中忘了自己。我不知道自己去了哪里，只顾盯着长满苔藓的地面走。这里没有路。我也不需要路。

人真正迷路时，自己总是知道的。我就是如此。此时已近午夜，而我离开母亲家门时还是正午。一轮满月照着我前行，在林地上投下交错缠绕的影子。 

终于，我来到一片平静的湖边。我在那里向春天之灵祈祷，向那位伟大的女神祈祷——所有五月女王都是仿照她的形象装扮的。“让我像塞莱斯特一样美丽吧，”我哭喊道，“让我也配当五月女王吧！”

湖水分开了。一道波浪轻拍水面。接着，那匹母马缓缓从水底爬出来，一只蹄子接着一只蹄子。那是一匹白色的母马，浑身湿透，猛烈地甩着头，把水珠从鬃毛上甩落。这一定是女神亲自化作凡间的形体，显现在我面前。它的鬃毛也编成了辫子，和塞莱斯特的头发一样，只是编进去的是苔草，而不是鲜花。

母马站在我面前，金色的眼睛注视着我。终于，它开口了（它的嘴并不能动，却仍然发出了声音）：“人类的孩子，你是来向我求助的吗？”

“是的，”我轻声说，“我想变得美丽。像塞莱斯特一样美丽。”

它向我低下硕大的头，用鼻子蹭了蹭我的手。我轻柔地抚摸它，感受着它呼在我指上的气息。祈祷得到了回应，突如其来的宽慰涌上心头，我把脸埋进它的鬃毛里，抽泣起来。

“别哭，人类的孩子，”它对我说，“到我幽暗的水中来，重获新生，成为一位属于你自己的女神。只要爬上我的背，我们就一起下去。你终会成为五月女王。”

我把它的鬃毛缠在手指上，用尽力气爬上它的背，把一条腿跨过它筋肉结实的侧腹。我们一起开始向水中下沉。我感到刺骨的冷水浸透了裙子和鞋子，坠得它们沉甸甸的；还没反应过来，水就已经漫到了胸口。 

就在那时，我往水下看去，心猛地一跳。那母马根本不是马，而是一具腐烂的庞然巨物，尸身上的皮肉一片片剥落，在水流中飘动。湿腐的死亡恶臭扑面而来，我一阵干呕。我伸手抓住唯一够得着的东西——一根伸到池塘上方的树枝——拼命往上拉。那怪物停止了下沉，转头朝向我。它的脸几乎只剩下一颗咧嘴的骷髅头，嵌着两只干瘪的眼睛。

一个名字涌到嘴边，化作一声哽住的尖叫：“溪马！”

“是——啊——”水里的东西嘶声说道。它马一样的嘴唇向后掀起，露出尖利的牙齿。

我转身想游开，却感觉那些牙齿咬住了我的背。月亮在高高的水面上方越变越小，渐渐远得无法触及。四周柔和的绿色包围了我。我沉向水底的苔藓。不。那不是苔藓。是残骸。而我最后看见的，是那道尖牙毕露的狞笑。

“你永远成不了女王，”它嘶哑地说，“不过，你的骨头一定会很美。”

我站在妈妈的小屋外，看着她经过。她转过头，对我微笑着喊道：“安娜！来跟我们一起跳舞吧！”她朝我伸出双手，系在手腕上的铃铛轻轻作响。毕竟，我们曾经是最好的朋友。

可走在她身旁的男孩们却嘲笑我。“丑八怪，小贱人！”其中一个尖声叫道。另一个扔来一块石头。“黄牙、呆脸、乱毛的废物！”还有一个拿着棍子朝我追来，像是要往我背上打，直到把棍子打断。

泪水盈满了我的眼睛，我退进树林。这里远离五月节游行的喧闹，一切都幽暗而寂静。树木像手指一样伸展在头顶，一时间，我在黑暗中忘了自己。我不知道自己去了哪里，只顾盯着长满苔藓的地面走。这里没有路。我也不需要路。

人真正迷路时，自己总是知道的。我就是如此。此时已近午夜，而我离开母亲家门时还是正午。一轮满月照着我前行，在林地上投下交错缠绕的影子。 

终于，我来到一片平静的湖边。我在那里向春天之灵祈祷，向那位伟大的女神祈祷——所有五月女王都是仿照她的形象装扮的。“让我像塞莱斯特一样美丽吧，”我哭喊道，“让我也配当五月女王吧！”

湖水分开了。一道波浪轻拍水面。接着，那匹母马缓缓从水底爬出来，一只蹄子接着一只蹄子。那是一匹白色的母马，浑身湿透，猛烈地甩着头，把水珠从鬃毛上甩落。这一定是女神亲自化作凡间的形体，显现在我面前。它的鬃毛也编成了辫子，和塞莱斯特的头发一样，只是编进去的是苔草，而不是鲜花。

母马站在我面前，金色的眼睛注视着我。终于，它开口了（它的嘴并不能动，却仍然发出了声音）：“人类的孩子，你是来向我求助的吗？”

“是的，”我轻声说，“我想变得美丽。像塞莱斯特一样美丽。”

它向我低下硕大的头，用鼻子蹭了蹭我的手。我轻柔地抚摸它，感受着它呼在我指上的气息。祈祷得到了回应，突如其来的宽慰涌上心头，我把脸埋进它的鬃毛里，抽泣起来。

“别哭，人类的孩子，”它对我说，“到我幽暗的水中来，重获新生，成为一位属于你自己的女神。只要爬上我的背，我们就一起下去。你终会成为五月女王。”

我把它的鬃毛缠在手指上，用尽力气爬上它的背，把一条腿跨过它筋肉结实的侧腹。我们一起开始向水中下沉。我感到刺骨的冷水浸透了裙子和鞋子，坠得它们沉甸甸的；还没反应过来，水就已经漫到了胸口。 

就在那时，我往水下看去，心猛地一跳。那母马根本不是马，而是一具腐烂的庞然巨物，尸身上的皮肉一片片剥落，在水流中飘动。湿腐的死亡恶臭扑面而来，我一阵干呕。我伸手抓住唯一够得着的东西——一根伸到池塘上方的树枝——拼命往上拉。那怪物停止了下沉，转头朝向我。它的脸几乎只剩下一颗咧嘴的骷髅头，嵌着两只干瘪的眼睛。

一个名字涌到嘴边，化作一声哽住的尖叫：“溪马！”

“是——啊——”水里的东西嘶声说道。它马一样的嘴唇向后掀起，露出尖利的牙齿。

我转身想游开，却感觉那些牙齿咬住了我的背。月亮在高高的水面上方越变越小，渐渐远得无法触及。四周柔和的绿色包围了我。我沉向水底的苔藓。不。那不是苔藓。是残骸。而我最后看见的，是那道尖牙毕露的狞笑。

“你永远成不了女王，”它嘶哑地说，“不过，你的骨头一定会很美。”

bindings.source: I... I did it. I actually saved him. Though it did not come without a cost, it meant so much to me to see him live beyond a fate that previously seemed inescapable. I know it's a temporary victory - at the end of these days it will all be reset, and then he will probably die many times, just as before. But now... at least I know something can be done.

bindings.source:
Irma is one of the most feared women in Elsinore for her quick temper. She's fiercely devoted to the Queen, and originally followed Gertrude from Bohemia, where she and Gertrude were both born and raised.

 Despite her teeth, I've seen that she has a warm side. She loves to gamble, and she's quite good; I wouldn't make a bet against her for all the world.
bindings.previous_target:
伊尔玛脾气急躁，是埃尔西诺最让人畏惧的女人之一。她对王后忠心耿耿，当年从波希米亚随乔特鲁德来到这里。她和乔特鲁德都在那里出生、长大。

虽然她很厉害，我也见过她温暖的一面。她喜欢赌博，而且很有一手；说什么我也不会跟她对赌。

bindings.source: King Hamlet's final notes mentioned Quince as 'The Playmaster.' He writes that Quince 'relieved' him of his eternal torment, which explains why he's a spirit in my world and no longer trapped in time. But if Quince has the power to do that, why hasn't he done it for me? What's clear is that all paths seem to lead to me finding this book--this 'Hand of Dionysus.' I'll need to do that before I can understand more.
bindings.previous_target: 哈姆雷特国王在最后的笔记中提到昆斯，称他为“戏班班主”。他写道，昆斯让他从永恒的折磨中“解脱”了。这解释了为什么他在我的世界里是个幽灵，不再被困在时间之中。可如果昆斯有这样的力量，为什么不对我这样做？ 有一点很清楚：所有的路似乎都指向找到那本书——那本《狄俄尼索斯之手》。我得先找到它，才能弄明白更多事情。

relationships.base:
I remember Celeste rode in the front.

She was the head of the May parade, wearing a long white dress with a blue ribbon around her waist and flowers braided into her hair. No one had ever seen a May Queen half so pretty, they said. A trail of wagons tied together proceeded down the only street in town and there she sat at the very front, skirts trailing beneath her legs, which dangled off the wagon's edge. Her feet were bare and pale and clean, her eyes a blue to match her sash. And even I had to admit she was beautiful.

I watched her go by from just outside mum's cottage. She turned to smile at me and called out. 'Anna! Come dance with us!' She extended her hands towards me, the bells tied to her wrists tinkling faintly. We had been best friends once, after all.

But the boys who walked at her side jeered at me. 'Ugly little bitch!' one of them screeched. Another tossed a stone. 'Brown-toothed, slack-jawed, scruff-haired nothing!' One of them came after me with a stick, as though he meant to break it over my back.

Tears filling my eyes, I retreated into the woods. Far away from the raucous sounds of the May Day parade, everything here was dark and silent. The trees stretched like fingers overhead, and for a moment I forgot myself in that darkness. I knew not where I went, but walked with my eyes locked upon the mossy ground. There was no path. I needed none.

All humans know when they have truly become lost. And so I had. It was nearly midnight now, though it had been noon when I left my mother's threshold. A full moon lit my path, casting twining shadows on the forest floor. 

At last I came upon a still lake. And there I prayed to the spirit of spring herself, that great goddess whose image all May Queens were created in. 'Make me beautiful like Celeste,' I cried. 'Make me worthy of being the May Queen, too!'

The waters parted. A single wave lapped the surface. And then, slowly, the mare climbed out of the water's depths, one hoof at a time. It was a white mare, drenched through, and it shook its head wildly, flicking drops of water from its mane. Surely this must be the goddess herself, manifested in mortal form. Its mane was braided -- just as Celeste's had been -- but with mossweed, not flowers.

The mare stood before me, its golden eyes fixed upon me. At last it said (with no mouth that could move, but with a voice all the same) 'Child of man, have you come to seek my aid?'

'I have,' I said, quietly. 'I want to be beautiful. As beautiful as Celeste.'

It bowed its great head to me and nuzzled my hand. I touched it tenderly, its breath on my fingers. And, flooded with sudden relief that my prayer had been answered, I pressed my face into its mane and sobbed.

'Cry not, child of man,' it told me. 'Come into my dark waters and be reborn as a goddess in your own right. Merely climb on my back, and we'll descend together. You shall be a May Queen yet.'

I wrapped its mane round my fingers and pulled myself up her back with all my might, swinging one leg over her sinewy side. Together, we began to descend into the water. I felt the cold bite of it weighing down my skirts, my shoes; and before I knew it, the water was up to my chest. 

It was then I peered beneath the surface and my heart leapt into my chest. The mare was no mare, but a rotted, hulking thing, its flesh stripped in pieces from its corpse and fluttering in the water's current. The wet stink of death came upon me, and I gagged. I reached for the only thing I could grab -- a branch overhanging the pond -- and pulled with all my might. The creature ceased its descent beneath the water and turned upon me, its face little more than two shriveled eyes in a grinning skull.

A name rose to my lips, a choked scream. 'Brook horse!'

'Yesssss,' the thing in the water hissed. Its horselike lips pulled back, revealing sharpened teeth.

I turned to swim, but felt those teeth closing down upon my back. The moon grew small, high above the surface, fading from reach. The soft green of it all surrounded me. I sank down to the moss at the bottom. No. Not moss. Remains. And the last thing I saw was that sharp, grinning smile.

'You shall never be Queen,' it rasped. 'But your bones shall be beautiful indeed.'

relationships.base: Grace and I spent the night together. I hope I see her again soon-- or perhaps, if there's a way out of this repeating world, that I might accept her offer to sail the world.

relationships.base: When I found Quince in the gallery, he spoke in riddles. Something about the nature and structure of a tragic work. Of course I've read many of the great tragedies-- and it sometimes feels like I'm living one-- but what does all that have to do with my predicament?

relationships.base: Marcellus has thirteen children, and grandchildren at that. I had no idea he was so-- er-- prolific. Then again, having to raise thirteen children would explain why nothing fazes him.
relationships.variant: Marcellus has thirteen children, and grandchildren at that. I had no idea he was so—er—prolific. Then again, having to raise thirteen children would explain why nothing fazes him.

relationships.base: I found King Hamlet's abandoned notes describing the end of his life. He was like me. But he gave up, and let madness consume him. He knew and understood everything that was happening around him-- his brother's plot against him, his wife turning from him-- and he couldn't stop it. Now he remains in Elsinore, neither alive nor fully dead. But why? Will that happen to me, too?

relationships.base: I've woken up in my bed again, but things feel - different. Strange.
relationships.variant: I've woken up in my bed again, but things feel—different. Strange.

relationships.base: My father was waiting, as usual, but not to chastise me -- rather, to invite me to some sort of feast in the Great Hall. I'll need to join everyone there.

relationships.base: I'd forgotten what it was like to see them all happy. This world -- this new world -- is this the world that would have been without the Book of Fates, without any of it?

relationships.base:
Irma is one of the most feared women in Elsinore for her quick temper. She's fiercely devoted to the Queen, and originally followed Gertrude from Bohemia, where she and Gertrude were both born and raised.

Despite her teeth, I've seen that she has a warm side. She loves to gamble, and she's quite good; I wouldn't make a bet against her for all the world.
